<!-- catalog-scope-summary:start -->
Here, **4DGS** covers native 4D Gaussians, deformable 3D Gaussians, explicit trajectories, and
related Gaussian representations for dynamic scenes.
<!-- catalog-scope-summary:end -->

Paper titles link to arXiv. `[page]` and `[code]` appear when available. Open
**Detailed contributions** for short summaries, tags, and code status.

## Reading guide

| If you are looking for...            | Start with                                                                        | What it covers                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Multi-view reconstruction            | [Multi-view reconstruction](#multi-view-dynamic-scene-reconstruction)             | Multi-camera methods plus reconstruction work not verified as exclusively monocular                  |
| Limited multi-view observations      | [Sparse multi-view reconstruction](#sparse-multi-view-reconstruction)             | Sparse-view, few-camera, two-image, and temporally sparse-frame reconstruction                       |
| Smaller or faster systems            | [Systems](#systems-compression-and-streaming)                                      | Compression, codecs, streaming, memory reduction, fast training, and rendering                       |
| Monocular reconstruction             | [Monocular reconstruction](#monocular-dynamic-scene-reconstruction)               | Methods whose verified capture regime is exclusively monocular                                       |
| Generalizable inference              | [Feed-forward 4DGS](#feed-forward-4dgs-and-world-models)                          | Methods that predict dynamic Gaussian representations without optimizing every scene from scratch    |
| New or controlled 4D content         | [Generation and editing](#4d-generation-and-editing)                              | Generation, animation, simulation, editing, control, and composition                                 |
| Motion and scene understanding       | [Tracking, segmentation, and SLAM](#dynamic-tracking-segmentation-and-slam)       | Persistent tracking, scene flow, segmentation, camera tracking, and dynamic mapping                  |
| People and articulated subjects      | [Dynamic humans and avatars](#dynamic-humans-and-avatars)                         | Bodies, heads, hands, relighting, animation, and human-object interaction                            |
| Evaluation papers and data           | [Evaluation studies](#evaluation-studies) and [datasets](#datasets)               | Evaluation studies plus recurring monocular, multi-view, human, driving, and physics datasets        |

Representation tags distinguish several common designs: `deformable-3dgs` uses canonical 3D
Gaussians with time-dependent deformation; `native-4dgs` gives primitives explicit spacetime
support; `explicit` stores trajectories, frames, or temporal bases directly; and `feed-forward`
predicts a representation without per-scene optimization. These tags overlap and describe design
choices rather than mutually exclusive paper families.

## Multi-view dynamic scene reconstruction

This is the default reconstruction lane. It includes verified multi-view methods, methods supporting
both monocular and multi-view input, and work not verified as exclusively monocular.

| [TruncGradGS: Improved 3D Gaussian Splatting via Truncated Gradient Updates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03534) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; dataset &middot; synthetic</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method, source</sub> | <ol><li>A piecewise truncated gradient replaces the near-zero tails of the 2D Gaussian spatial derivative with a linear surrogate outside the density isocontour, matched to the true derivative at the boundary (content/3_method/truncated_grad.tex:17-74).</li><li>The surrogate is gated to dead Gaussians with negative alpha gradient, paired with tile-radius padding, interleaved density-control phases and delayed pruning (content/3_method/truncated_grad.tex:173-223).</li><li>It is applied on top of static 3DGS and 2DGS and dynamic 4DGS, CEM-4DGS and 4D-Scaffold, alongside a new six-scene synthetic multi-view 4D benchmark (content/4_eval/main.tex:15-26,76-78).</li></ol> |
| [EvoGS: Modeling Deformation Evolution for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00994) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; per-scene &middot; multi-view &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>Maintains a persistent per-Gaussian deformation buffer and extrapolates each current deformation from that Gaussian own corrected history (sections/4_method_part2.tex:6-39).</li><li>Corrects that extrapolated prior with an MLP observation through a learned gain read from residual memory, velocity magnitudes and angular deviation (sections/4_method_part3.tex:19-42).</li><li>Gates densification on deformation residual and angle, then clones or splits after displacing the parent along its corrected deformation (sections/4_method_part3.tex:46-69).</li></ol> |
| [ATGS: Anchored Temporal Gaussian Splatting for Long Volumetric Video Representation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30184) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/WuJH2001/ATGS "Project page")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; hybrid &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>A time-conditioned anchor carrying a position, a 64-dimensional feature, a spatial scale and a keyframe index, so anchors rather than Gaussian trajectories localize motion in space and time (3_method.tex:27-33, e-anchor).</li><li>A temporal windowing strategy activating only anchors whose keyframe index lies within a window of size W (default 7) around the queried time, which the source credits with reduced temporal jitter (3_method.tex:39-59, e-window).</li><li>Hierarchical anchor features, a per-anchor feature plus a shared 128-cubed spatial grid plus M segment-wise 4D hash grids, decoded into per-time Temporal Gaussians .</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [LagrangeGS: Non-Conservative Lagrangian System on Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22773) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; physics-aware &middot; continuous-time &middot; editing</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>Formulates dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting as a non-conservative Lagrangian system, approximating the velocity-Hessian as the identity so per-particle acceleration reduces to a closed form and no 3M-dimensional system has to be solved per integration step.</li><li>Restricts the learned non-conservative force to be explicitly time independent and adds a differentiable Kabsch local rigid alignment over each particle's k-nearest-neighbour support, targeting backward integration and geometric stability during long rollouts.</li><li>Distils trajectories from a pre-trained DefGS or FreeGave model.</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [Learning Implicit Constitutive Laws for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting from Monocular Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22102) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; depth-prior &middot; physics-aware &middot; multi-view</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: category, datasets, experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>GCA learns an implicit neural constitutive law for a deformable object from a single fixed-viewpoint video, LoRA-adapting NCLaw elasticity and plasticity networks on top of 3D Gaussians initialized from a separate static multi-view scan.</li><li>Rank-based Depth-Geometric Anchors supervise geometry by a scale-invariant Spearman rank correlation between rendered and estimated depth, kept only for correspondences outside a morphologically derived edge band that pass a correlation threshold.</li><li>A Constitutive Prior Regularizer fits four elastic and four plastic classical models to the network outputs on a fixed 256-particle subset, penalizing deviation weighted by inverse parameter variance as a soft prior.</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [Towards Alias-Free 4D Gaussian Representations with Motion-Aware Filtering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21828) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://maaf-4dgs.github.io/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/val-iisc/MAAF-4DGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; native-4dgs &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; per-scene &middot; synthetic</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces a motion-aware 3D smoothing filter for 4D Gaussian representations that replaces Mip-Splatting's constant per-primitive sampling rate with one varying per timestamp, so band-limiting tracks each primitive's motion.</li><li>Estimates each primitive's joint density over discrete time and focal-length-to-depth ratio by Parzen-window estimation with a Weibull kernel and a Gaussian kernel, then takes the conditional mode at the query time.</li><li>Single-scale training with multi-scale testing on Neural 3D Video and D-NeRF, and shows the filter is representation-agnostic by attaching it to both SARO-GS and SpeeDe3DGS.</li></ol> |
| [ERF-GS: Reconstructing Fast Motion from Disjoint Event-RGB Viewpoints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08531) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/andrewbxy/ERF-GS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; fast-motion &middot; per-scene &middot; dataset-release</sub> | <ol><li>EARL, an event-assisted regularized loss that supervises two rendered images against an event frame instead of a ground-truth RGB frame, adding confidence weighting by event magnitude plus linear-trajectory and colour regularizers.</li><li>EDS, an event-guided densification strategy that unprojects nonzero event pixels along sampled depths, cross-validates candidates against K other event views, then filters by depth uniqueness, spatial coherence and deformation consistency.</li><li>Neu3D and Nvidia variants curated with v2e-simulated events, temporal subsampling, simulated motion blur and disjoint RGB/event viewpoints, on which ERF-GS gains 0.91 dB and 1.44 dB average DPSNR over its 4DGS backbone.</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [FAST-GS: Frequency Aware Space-time Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Dynamic Novel View Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01958) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; native-4dgs &middot; real-time &middot; fast-motion</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>Replaces the polynomial motion model of 4DGS with a per-axis Fourier series of order five for each Gaussian centre, separating low-frequency global trajectory from high-frequency local detail.</li><li>Adds a motion regularization loss weighting the i-th Fourier coefficient pair by i squared, a low-pass penalty that damps high-frequency jitter while preserving low-frequency coherence.</li><li>The best PSNR among Gaussian baselines on three of four N3V scenes, including 34.65 dB on Sear Steak; a separate Google Immersive scene supplies the only speed figure, 146 FPS.</li></ol> |
| [StructureGS: Structure-aware Gaussian Splatting for Articulated Object Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26889) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; explicit &middot; robotics</sub> | <ol><li>Reconstructs articulated objects with explicit part structure rather than relying on photometric supervision alone.</li><li>Uses oriented part bounding boxes to constrain spatial coherence and preserve contact between adjacent movable parts.</li><li>Adds structure-aware losses that sharpen part boundaries and reduce geometric artifacts during Gaussian optimization.</li></ol> |
| [GrainGS: Gradient-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Dynamic Novel View Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21448) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/I2-Multimedia-Lab/GrainGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; multi-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; real-time &middot; synthetic</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>GrainGS combines a hierarchical anchor scaffold with per-Gaussian deformation.</li><li>A static warm-up stage first establishes a time-invariant canonical representation from observations across all timestamps.</li></ol> |
| [Implicit 4D Gaussian Splatting for Fast Motion with Large Inter-Frame Displacements](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12362) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://seung-gyeom.github.io/SPIN-4DGS/ "Project page") [![Non-functional or unverified GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-8c959f?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/seung-gyeom/SPIN-4DGS "Placeholder or documentation-only GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; per-scene &middot; native-4dgs &middot; explicit &middot; fast-motion</sub> | <ol><li>Learns Gaussian attributes from explicitly collected spatiotemporal positions instead of modeling temporal displacements.</li><li>Uses a lightweight feed-forward network under rasterization-based reconstruction loss to avoid optimizing attributes explicitly at every spatiotemporal position.</li><li>Shares representations across Gaussians to improve spatiotemporal consistency under large inter-frame motion.</li></ol> |
| [Grassmannian Splatting I: Moving rank-2 Spacetime Surfels for Dynamic Scene Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10489) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/PaulCelanCoding/grassmannian-splatting "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; native-4dgs &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces Grassmannian splatting, whose Gaussian primitives lie on rank-three planes in spacetime and condition to rank-two surfels at each frame.</li><li>Encodes primitive orientation, normal velocity, disk shape, and tangential drift in a closed-form motion model without a learned deformation field.</li><li>Uses a standard 3DGS rasterizer.</li></ol> |

| [MVFusion-GS: Motion-Variance Guided Temporal Attention for High-Quality Dynamic Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01578) (2026)<br><br>[![Non-functional or unverified GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-8c959f?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/toseeai-com/MVFusion-GS "Placeholder or documentation-only GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Aggregates per-Gaussian deformation statistics over time to estimate motion variance and guide dynamic-static separation.</li><li>Applies temporal self-attention over neighboring timestamps to model local motion dependencies.</li></ol> |
| [SemDynReg: Semantics-Guided Deformation Regularization for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28656) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://dyn-reg-3dgs.github.io/ "Project page")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; segmentation &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces a semantics-guided framework that enforces dynamic regularization at the object level, aiming to achieve spatially consistent object-wise deformation.</li><li>Firsts extract segmentation masks using the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and derive semantic features from input images.</li></ol> |
| [Temporally Aware Densification for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23212) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://vikramsandu.github.io/publications/TADGS/index.html "Project page")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; native-4dgs &middot; fast-motion</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces visibility-aware densification so Gaussians are refined according to their actual temporal presence.</li><li>Adjusts each Gaussian's densification threshold according to its temporal lifespan through temporally adaptive thresholding.</li><li>Uses temporal offset warping to increase deformation capacity near temporal centers and improve reconstruction of highly dynamic regions.</li></ol> |
| [Multi4D: High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Multi-Level Competitive Allocation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22197) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://batfacewayne.github.io/Multi4D.io/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/BatFaceWayne/Multi4D "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; per-scene &middot; hybrid &middot; tracking &middot; segmentation</sub> | <ol><li>Represents a dynamic scene with static, persistent, and transient Gaussian subsets tailored to different temporal behaviors.</li><li>Exposes persistent Gaussians as stable primitives for efficient segmentation and tracking in addition to novel-view synthesis.</li></ol> |

| [One World, Dual Timeline: Decoupled Spatio-Temporal Gaussian Scene Graph for 4D Cooperative Driving Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07910) (2026)<br><br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; driving &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>DUST-GSG gives each dynamic agent one shared canonical Gaussian set and deformation field but two source-specific SE(3) pose trajectories, so vehicle and infrastructure cameras render it at their own capture timestamps (neurips_2026.tex:305-330).</li><li>Theorem 1 bounds the single-timeline photometric loss below by \|dtau\|^2\|\|v\|\|^2/4 times summed per-Gaussian Fisher eigenvalues, and shows the decoupled form admits a zero-loss solution with independently optimising poses (neurips_2026.tex:337-380).</li><li>A static-anchor stage Hungarian-matches co-visible static vehicles and solves a 6-DoF SE(3) correction by L-BFGS on box-corner error, with smoothness and drift regularisers stabilising joint optimisation (neurips_2026.tex:423-456, 458-517).</li></ol> |
| [FreeTimeGS++: Secrets of Dynamic Gaussian Splatting and Their Principles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03337) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://yklcs.com/ftgspp "Project page")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; per-scene &middot; native-4dgs &middot; explicit</sub> | <ol><li>Builds a controlled baseline to isolate and analyze training heuristics that materially affect dynamic Gaussian splatting quality.</li><li>Uses duration-aware temporal partitioning plus photometric and motion discrepancies to organize dynamic primitives.</li><li>Combines gated marginalization with neural velocity fields to improve stability, reproducibility, and reconstruction quality.</li></ol> |
| [Color-Encoded Illumination for High-Speed Volumetric Scene Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26920) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://davidnovikov.github.io/color-encoded-illumination-website/ "Project page")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; fast-motion</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>Color-coded strobed illumination encodes N high-speed interframes into each low-speed frame of unaugmented multi-view cameras .</li><li>Strobed Gaussian-Flow: dynamic 3DGS with time-dependent deformations rendered per interframe, mixed by the known LED color dictionary, and fit to the captured RGB frames with an L1 plus inverse-depth TV loss.</li><li>Hardware prototype (8 IDS cameras, Arduino-driven RGB LED strobing, PWM color dictionary) with real high-speed captures and a simulation study of interframe count, ambient light, albedo, camera count and motion complexity.</li></ol> |

| [TrackerSplat: Exploiting Point Tracking for Fast and Robust Dynamic 3D Gaussians Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02586) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/yindaheng98/TrackerSplat "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; tracking &middot; multi-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; fast-motion &middot; fast-training</sub> | <ol><li>Uses off-the-shelf point tracking to improve dynamic 3D Gaussian reconstruction under large inter-frame displacements.</li><li>Triangulates per-view pixel trajectories onto Gaussians to guide their relocation, rotation, and scale before optimization.</li><li>Enables parallel processing of adjacent frames while aiming to preserve rendering quality.</li></ol> |
| [TRiGS: Temporal Rigid-Body Motion for Scalable 4D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00538) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://wwwjjn.github.io/TRiGS-project_page/ "Project page")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; native-4dgs &middot; explicit &middot; continuous-time</sub> | <ol><li>Models per-primitive motion with coupled SE(3) transformations instead of fragmented piecewise-linear trajectories.</li><li>Adds hierarchical Bézier residuals and learnable local anchors to represent complex nonlinear rigid-body motion.</li><li>Preserves temporal identity and limits Gaussian proliferation over 600–1200-frame sequences.</li></ol> |

| [Periodic Vibration Gaussian: Dynamic Urban Scene Reconstruction and Real-time Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18561) (2023)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://fudan-zvg.github.io/PVG/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/fudan-zvg/PVG "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>multi-view-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; driving &middot; real-time &middot; per-scene &middot; depth-prior</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>Periodic Vibration Gaussian: a primitive whose mean vibrates sinusoidally about a learned life peak and whose opacity decays away from it, letting static and dynamic urban content share one formulation.</li><li>A temporal smoothing scheme that replaces optical-flow supervision by translating each point by an opacity-weighted average velocity, and a position-aware control rule scaling densification thresholds with distance from the scene centre.</li><li>Waymo and KITTI evaluation against S-NeRF, StreetSurf, Mars, 3DGS, NSG, SUDS and EmerNeRF, reporting 28.11 novel-view PSNR on Waymo at 50 FPS against EmerNeRF 0.053.</li></ol> |

## Sparse multi-view reconstruction

This category is reserved for sparse views, few cameras, two-image input, or sparse temporal
observations under the multi-view-priority rule. Monocular-only work remains in the dedicated
monocular category.

| [UniFusion: Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction via Unified Spatio-temporal Depth Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05888) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://yongzhelyu.github.io/UniFusion/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; surface-gaussian &middot; depth-prior</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>Represents the monocular depths of all views and time steps as per-view spatio-temporal neural fields optimized jointly, replacing the separate spatial and temporal alignment stages of prior sparse-view 4D work (sec/1_introduction.tex:68-69).</li><li>Carries temporal variation as per-timestep residual MLP weights factored by vector-matrix decomposition at rank 8, so no foreground segmentation or point-tracking model is needed (sec/3_method.tex:76-105).</li><li>Adds a multi-view depth-order hinge loss on cross-view reprojected depth, then uses the aligned depths to initialize and supervise deformable 2DGS and MonoFusion backends (sec/3_method.tex:116-133, sec/3_method.tex:168-172).</li></ol> |
| [D²-4DGS: Dual-Depth Guided Sparse-Camera 4D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01588) (2026)<br><br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; depth-prior &middot; native-4dgs &middot; per-scene</sub> | <ol><li>D²-4DGS folds monocular and multi-view geometric depth priors into Gaussian structure optimization for view synthesis from two to four calibrated cameras.</li><li>Aligns monocular depth to COLMAP multi-view depth per frame and view with a positive scale and shift, then keeps only pixels whose relative disagreement stays below a threshold as verified geometric anchors.</li><li>Turns depth evidence into explicit structure updates: prior-supported pixels seed densification in under-reconstructed regions, while contribution-weighted depth inconsistency and visibility-aware opacity prune persistently unstable Gaussians.</li></ol> |
| [FillGS: Filling Observation Gaps in 4D Gaussian Splatting via Viewpoint-Time Selection and Generative Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29284) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://otonari726.github.io/fillgs/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; multi-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; uncertainty</sub> | <ol><li>Actively selects spatiotemporal virtual viewpoints for generative 4DGS refinement in two stages: rendering sensitivity ranks observed viewpoints as exploration starts, then a motion-aware deficiency score, per-Gaussian speed over observation count, ranks the virtual candidates.</li><li>Fine-tunes 4DGS on refined images using RoMa v2 matching-confidence consistency masks and motion-aware co-visibility weights that down-weight generated pixels wherever a region is unreliable or already well observed.</li><li>Introduces sparse-observation splits of 6 Neural 3D Video and 5 Technicolor scenes that train on two cameras and evaluate separately on interpolation and extrapolation test views.</li></ol> |
| [4D Human-Scene Reconstruction from Low-Overlap Captures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09125) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://sisyphm.github.io/studiorecon-page/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; human &middot; sparse-view</sub> | <ol><li>Reconstructs dynamic human scenes from sparse, low-overlap cameras by separating the background and people into complementary Gaussian representations.</li><li>Densifies background supervision by synthesizing hundreds of camera-controlled views with a video diffusion model.</li><li>Initializes deformable humans through cross-view identity association and triangulated keypoints, then harmonizes the composed scene with motion-adaptive diffusion refinement.</li></ol> |
| [World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01202) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/amri/projects/world-from-motion/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; multi-view &middot; generation &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Enables generating freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian representations from monocular videos.</li><li>Builds a dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3DGS representations, with simulated artifacts characteristic of monocular reconstruction.</li><li>Conditions a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion along both input and target camera trajectories to correct rendering artifacts and fill in missing regions.</li></ol> |
| [HiReFF: High-Resolution Feedforward Human Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Sparse-View Video](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29333) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://iridescentjiang.github.io/HiReFF "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/IridescentJiang/HiReFF "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; sparse-view &middot; unposed &middot; feed-forward &middot; streaming</sub> | <ol><li>Uses feed-forward for 2K-resolution 360° human video reconstruction from uncalibrated sparse-view videos.</li><li>Decomposes the pipeline into foreground 3D Gaussian reconstruction from sparse-view videos (four views separated by 90°) and computationally efficient high-resolution synthesis.</li></ol> |
| [4C4D: 4 Camera 4D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04063) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://junshengzhou.github.io/4C4D/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/yangzf-1023/4C4D "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; native-4dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Targets 4D Gaussian reconstruction from video captured by as few as four portable cameras.</li><li>Introduces a neural decaying function on Gaussian opacities to focus 4DGS gradients more strongly on geometry learning.</li><li>Addresses the geometry-versus-appearance learning imbalance in sparse-camera settings.</li></ol> |
| [UFO-4D: Unposed Feedforward 4D Reconstruction from Two Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.24290) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://ufo-4d.github.io/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ufo-4d/ufo-4d "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; feed-forward &middot; two-view &middot; unposed &middot; self-supervised &middot; explicit</sub> | <ol><li>Reconstructs a dense explicit 4D representation from two unposed images in a unified feed-forward framework.</li><li>Jointly estimates dynamic Gaussian geometry, 3D motion, and camera pose.</li><li>Renders multiple signals from shared Gaussians, coupling appearance, depth, and motion for self-supervised image-synthesis training.</li></ol> |
| [SV-GS: Sparse View 4D Reconstruction with Skeleton-Driven Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00285) (2026)<br><br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; multi-view &middot; sparse-view &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; generation</sub> | <ol><li>Simultaneously estimates a deformation model and the object's motion over time under sparse observations.</li><li>Uses a rough skeleton graph and an initial static reconstruction to guide motion estimation under sparse observations.</li><li>Improves PSNR by up to 34% on synthetic sparse-view data and matches dense monocular-video methods on real data.</li></ol> |
| [Next Best View Selections for Semantic and Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22771) (2025)<br><br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; segmentation &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Formulates the view selection problem as an active learning problem, where the goal is to prioritize frames that provide the greatest information gain for model training.</li><li>Introduces an active learning algorithm with Fisher Information that quantifies the informativeness of candidate views with respect to both semantic Gaussian parameters and deformation networks.</li></ol> |
| [DGGT: Feedforward 4D Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes using Unposed Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03004) (2025)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://xiaomi-research.github.io/dggt/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/xiaomi-research/dggt "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; feed-forward &middot; unposed &middot; sparse-view &middot; driving &middot; native-4dgs</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Reformulates camera pose as a model output for pose-free, single-pass driving-scene reconstruction from sparse images.</li><li>Jointly predicts per-frame Gaussian maps and camera parameters, with dynamic and lifespan heads for motion and temporal visibility.</li></ol> |

| [Geometry-Consistent 4D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-Input Dynamic View Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23044) (2025)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://liyw420.github.io/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/liyw420/GC-4DGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; sparse-view &middot; native-4dgs &middot; depth-prior</sub> | <ol><li>Detects dynamically inconsistent multi-view-stereo estimates before they corrupt sparse-input 4D reconstruction.</li><li>Regularizes geometry with global and local depth constraints derived from monocular depth predictions.</li></ol> |
| [Sparse4DGS: 4D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-Frame Dynamic Scene Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07122) (2025)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://changyueshi.github.io/Sparse4DGS/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; depth-prior &middot; sparse-frame</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Targets dynamic reconstruction from temporally sparse frames, where large gaps make deformation estimation underconstrained.</li><li>Aligns texture and depth cues through texture-aware deformation regularization to stabilize motion between observed frames.</li><li>Uses texture-aware canonical optimization to preserve fine appearance while filling unobserved temporal intervals.</li></ol> |
| [Splatography: Sparse multi-view dynamic Gaussian Splatting for filmmaking challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.05152) (2025)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://azzarelli.github.io/splatographypage/index.html "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; online &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; segmentation &middot; sparse-view</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Splits the canonical Gaussians and deformation field into foreground and background components using a sparse set of masks for frames at t=0.</li><li>Produces SotA qualitative and quantitative results; up to 3 PSNR higher with half the model size on 3-D scenes.</li><li>Each representation is separately trained on different loss functions during canonical pre-training.</li></ol> |
| [PhysTwin: Physics-Informed Reconstruction and Simulation of Deformable Objects from Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17973) (2025)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://jianghanxiao.github.io/phystwin-web/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; rgb-d &middot; physics-aware &middot; robotics &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>Physics-informed digital twin of a deformable object from three RGB-D videos: a spring-mass model for dynamics, a TRELLIS shape prior for complete geometry, and isotropic 3D Gaussians for appearance.</li><li>Hierarchical sparse-to-dense inverse modeling: CMA-ES zero-order search over topology and sparse physical parameters, then first-order refinement of dense spring stiffness and collision parameters in a differentiable spring-mass simulator.</li><li>Gaussians optimized at the first frame are deformed per timestep by LBS from neighboring mass nodes; evaluated on the authors' 22-scenario interaction dataset for resimulation, future prediction and unseen interactions.</li></ol> |
| [Physically Plausible Human–Object Rendering From Sparse Views via 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09640) (2025)<br><br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; human &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; physics-aware &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>HOGS renders human-object interactions from 6 fixed sparse views by composing LBS-deformed human Gaussians (with an MLP-modulated skinning field) and rigidly transformed object Gaussians.</li><li>Physical plausibility is enforced directly on Gaussians: a contact loss pulls predicted contact regions together and a separation loss penalizes human Gaussians whose means fall inside a precomputed object SDF.</li><li>Pre-trained sparse-view pose refiner and contact predictor support the per-scene optimization; +3.4 dB PSNR over MANUS on HODome at 162 FPS, and extension to MANUS-Grasps hand-object rendering.</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [Spatiotemporal Gaussian Optimization for 4D Cone Beam CT Reconstruction from Sparse Projections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04140) (2025)<br><br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; radiative-imaging &middot; sparse-view &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: datasets, experiments, links, method, resources, source</sub> | <ol><li>Optimize a spatiotemporal Gaussian anatomy representation against measured X-ray projections using a joint deformation network.</li></ol> |
| [DynSUP: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting From an Unposed Image Pair](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00851) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://colin-de.github.io/DynSUP/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; two-view &middot; unposed &middot; explicit &middot; driving</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Object-level dense two-view bundle adjustment decomposes a dynamic scene into piece-wise rigid parts and jointly estimates relative camera motion and per-object motion to initialize dynamic Gaussians from two unposed images.</li><li>SE(3)-field-driven Gaussian splatting: every Gaussian carries its own learnable rigid transform, initialized from object-level motion and regularized toward per-object coherence; frame 0 renders untransformed, frame 1 transformed.</li><li>Test-time alignment optimizes camera pose and per-object SE(3) interpolation ratios; on KITTI and Kubric two-frame pairs the method beats InstantSplat, 4DGS and SC-GS on PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS.</li></ol> |
| [SplatFields: Neural Gaussian Splats for Sparse 3D and 4D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11211) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://markomih.github.io/SplatFields/ "Project page")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; multi-view &middot; real-time &middot; sparse-view</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces an optimization strategy that effectively regularizes splat features by modeling them as the outputs of a corresponding implicit neural field.</li><li>This results in a consistent enhancement of reconstruction quality across various scenarios.</li></ol> |
| [TOGS: Gaussian Splatting with Temporal Opacity Offset for Real-Time 4D DSA Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19586) (2024)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/hustvl/TOGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>sparse-reconstruction &middot; sparse-view &middot; real-time &middot; radiative-imaging</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces TOGS, a Gaussian splatting method with opacity offset over time, which can effectively improve the rendering quality and speed of 4D DSA.</li><li>Introduces an opacity offset table for each Gaussian to model the opacity offsets of the Gaussian, using these opacity-varying Gaussians to model the temporal variations in the radiance of the contrast agent.</li><li>By interpolating the opacity offset table, the opacity variation of the Gaussian at different time points can be determined.</li></ol> |

| Paper (arXiv) | Key contributions |
| --- | --- |
| [CC-4DGS: Computational Deformation and Point-Cloud Compression for Storage-Efficient Dynamic Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02184) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/KyungdaePark/CC-4DGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; compression &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>Replaces the learnable hash tables of prior deformation-field 4DGS with a computational deformation field that hashes voxel corners through parallel universal hash functions and decodes the dense signature per level on the fly (Sections/Method.tex:42-53).</li><li>Compresses canonical Gaussian attributes with CCA: SH-AC through a geometry-conditioned autoencoder plus a 256-entry residual codebook, scalars at 12-bit quantization, mu-law companding for the dynamic indicator, Zstandard packing (Sections/Method.tex:152-173).</li><li>N3DV Deform-module storage of 1.9 MB against 68.4 MB for Swift4D and 221.1 MB for Grid4D, keeping rendering real time via vertex reuse and a cached time-invariant spatial feature (Sections/Performance_Evaluation.tex:166-172).</li></ol> |
| [Amortized Anchor Refinement for Deployable Continuous-Time 4D Gaussian Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30218) (2026)<br><br>[![Non-functional or unverified GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-8c959f?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Jingong-Chen/Amortized-Anchor-Refinement "Placeholder or documentation-only GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; native-4dgs &middot; per-scene &middot; compression &middot; streaming</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments, method</sub> | <ol><li>A frozen VGGT-Omega backbone grounds K=2 Gaussians per input-view ray at its predicted depth, so per-scene optimization refines geometry instead of searching for it (sec/3method.tex:59-93).</li><li>Capacity Constrained Refinement replaces densify-and-prune with an opacity-ranked floor of N_min Gaussians, reported to lift walk from 20.48 to 24.22 dB while bounding memory (sec/3method.tex:122-142).</li><li>Persistent Homology Pruning and Compression prunes to a transmission budget under a persistence constraint and codes trajectories at 10 bits, giving 1.4-2.8 MB packages a Quest Pro decodes at 87 fps (sec/3method.tex:165-239).</li></ol> |
| [SACHA: Semantic-Aware Compression for 3D Gaussian Head Avatars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23133) (2026)<br><br><sub>efficiency &middot; compression &middot; human &middot; multi-view &middot; mesh-anchored &middot; per-scene</sub> | <ol><li>Decomposes a dynamic Gaussian head avatar into a canonical Gaussian asset coded once with its FLAME binding indices and per-frame FLAME parameters, split into static and dynamic components and CABAC-coded, that carry all motion.</li><li>Adds semantic-aware density control: a region-wise modulator, the ratio of global to region-level learned perceptual sensitivity, rescales the densification threshold and pruning ratio of each of eight FLAME mask regions within fixed bounds.</li><li>Introduces a perceptual importance score extending LightGaussian's measure with a pixel-level reference sensitivity map and a learned per-Gaussian sensitivity, used to rank primitives for removal independently inside each semantic region.</li></ol> |
| [S$^2$GS: Structured Sparse Gaussian Streaming for Efficient Free-Viewpoint Video Reconstruction on Edge-IoT Devices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19639) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/liyw420/S2GS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; online &middot; streaming &middot; fast-training &middot; real-time</sub> | <ol><li>Organises per-frame Gaussian residuals on a streaming octree that is fixed after the first frame, giving logarithmic residual lookup and removing the online pruning and densification of prior streaming methods.</li><li>Gates residual updates per octree region: max-pooled viewspace-gradient confidences, Gumbel-Sigmoid relaxation, and a multi-level straight-through estimator rounding to one decimal place instead of binary, which the paper reports avoids gate collapse.</li><li>Streaming FVV results on N3DV, Meet Room and ENeRF Outdoor on an RTX 4090, plus Jetson AGX Orin and nine-camera telerobotic-testbed deployments with per-frame power and energy.</li></ol> |
| [QuARC-GS: Quantized Anchored Residual Coding for Compact Dynamic Scene Streaming with Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18285) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/high-performance-computational-optics/QuARC-GS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; online &middot; streaming &middot; compression &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; multi-view</sub> | <ol><li>Quantization-aware anchor deformation rounds per-anchor 6-DoF motion residuals with a straight-through estimator during training, so near-static anchors collapse to the identity and the entropy coder captures sparsity without a transmitted mask.</li><li>Change-gated densification adds new Gaussians only where the view-space gradient of the consecutive-frame photometric-loss difference is large; the N3DV ablation cuts Gaussians added per frame from 468 to 153.</li><li>The lowest per-frame storage in both comparison tables, 36 KB on N3DV and 18 KB on MeetRoom, at 32.16 dB and 30.67 dB PSNR, against ReCon-GS at 400 KB and 300 KB.</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [ACA-GS: Adaptive-Capacity Anchored Gaussian Splatting for Compact Dynamic Radiance Fields](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04581) (2026)<br><br><sub>efficiency &middot; compression &middot; multi-view &middot; hybrid &middot; real-time &middot; fast-motion</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>Adaptive Anchor Cardinality relocates low-importance Neural Gaussians between anchors using opacity accumulated across training views, letting each anchor host a variable primitive count without spawning new anchors.</li><li>Adaptive Anchor Feature Masking learns per-anchor binary masks over a maskable feature segment, with a conditional regularization loss that suppresses sparsification wherever time-dependent features are active.</li><li>Reduces storage 35-42% versus GIFStream on MPEG, Panoptic Sports and N3DV (3.5, 7.3 and 6.3 MB) at comparable quality, reaching roughly 1.5x higher compression on fast-motion MPEG sequences.</li></ol> |

| [Temporally Compressed 3D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05700) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://ahmad-jarrar.github.io/tc-3dgs/ "Project page")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; per-scene &middot; explicit &middot; compression</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Prunes Gaussians using temporal relevance and applies gradient-aware mixed-precision quantization to dynamic attributes.</li><li>Compresses Gaussian trajectories with Ramer–Douglas–Peucker keypoint selection and interpolation.</li><li>Up to 67-fold compression with minimal or no loss of visual quality.</li></ol> |
| [QUEEN: QUantized Efficient ENcoding of Dynamic Gaussians for Streaming Free-viewpoint Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04469) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/amri/projects/queen/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/NVlabs/QUEEN "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; online &middot; streaming &middot; compression &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Encodes a dynamic sequence as Gaussian-attribute residuals between consecutive frames instead of retransmitting complete representations.</li><li>Quantizes non-position attributes with a latent decoder and sparsifies position residuals with learned gating.</li><li>Uses view-space gradient changes to identify dynamic content, reporting about 0.7 MB per frame, under five-second training, and 350 FPS rendering.</li></ol> |
| [4D Scaffold Gaussian Splatting with Dynamic-Aware Anchor Growing for Efficient and High-Fidelity Dynamic Scene Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17044) (2024)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/raikuma/4D-Scaffold-GS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; compression &middot; native-4dgs</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces a 4D anchor-based framework that tackles the storage cost in different perspective.</li><li>Retains a sufficient quantity to accurately model dynamic contents, while compressing them into compact, grid-aligned 4D anchor features.</li></ol> |
| [Dynamics-Aware Gaussian Splatting Streaming Towards Fast On-the-Fly 4D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.14847) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://www.liuzhening.top/DASS "Project page")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; online &middot; streaming &middot; fast-training &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Uses selective inheritance to carry reliable Gaussians between timestamps and preserve temporal continuity during online reconstruction.</li><li>Introduces a dynamics-aware shift that separates static and dynamic primitives and moves the dynamic subset efficiently.</li><li>Applies error-guided densification to emerging content.</li></ol> |
| [HiCoM: Hierarchical Coherent Motion for Streamable Dynamic Scene with 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07541) (2024)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gqk/HiCoM "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; online &middot; streaming &middot; compression &middot; fast-training</sub> | <ol><li>Builds a compact initial representation with perturbation smoothing, then learns nonuniform motion through hierarchical local Gaussian coherence.</li><li>Merges newly added Gaussians into the representation while removing an equal number of low-opacity primitives to constrain stream size.</li><li>About 85% lower storage, roughly 20% higher learning efficiency, and under two seconds per frame with parallel processing.</li></ol> |
| **[New]** [LoDAvatar: Hierarchical Embedding and Selective Detail Enhancement for Adaptive Levels of Detail Gaussian Avatars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20789) (2024)<br><br><sub>efficiency &middot; explicit &middot; human &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: datasets, experiments, links, method, resources, source</sub> | <ol><li>Hierarchical embedding and selective detail enhancement provide adaptive levels of detail for drivable Gaussian avatars.</li><li>Objective and subjective evaluations compare visual quality and computational rendering costs across detail levels.</li></ol> |
| [MEGA: Memory-Efficient 4D Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13613) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://xinjie-q.github.io/MEGA "Project page") [![Non-functional or unverified GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-8c959f?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Xinjie-Q/MEGA "Placeholder or documentation-only GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; per-scene &middot; native-4dgs &middot; compression &middot; explicit</sub> | <ol><li>Replaces high-dimensional per-Gaussian spherical-harmonic color attributes with direct color and a shared lightweight color predictor.</li><li>Introduces entropy-constrained Gaussian deformation and opacity-based entropy loss to limit Gaussian count.</li><li>Combines the representation with half-precision storage and zip compression.</li></ol> |
| [V^3: Viewing Volumetric Videos on Mobiles via Streamable 2D Dynamic Gaussians](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13648) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://authoritywang.github.io/v3/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AuthorityWang/VideoGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; explicit &middot; streaming &middot; compression &middot; real-time</sub> | <ol><li>Rearranges dynamic Gaussian attributes as multi-channel 2D video so standard hardware video codecs can stream them to mobile devices.</li><li>Uses hash-encoded motion, Gaussian pruning, and entropy-temporal refinement to disentangle motion and appearance while reducing storage.</li><li>Provides multi-platform players that decode and render streamed volumetric video on common devices.</li></ol> |
| [Robust Dual Gaussian Splatting for Immersive Human-centric Volumetric Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.08353) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://nowheretrix.github.io/DualGS/ "Project page")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; human &middot; real-time &middot; compression &middot; tracking &middot; generation</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces a Gaussian-based approach, dubbed DualGS, for real-time and playback of complex human performance with excellent compression ratios.</li><li>Employs a coarse-to-fine training strategy for frame-by-frame human performance modeling.</li><li>Achieves a compression ratio of up to 120 times, only requiring approximately 350KB of storage per frame.</li></ol> |
| [SwinGS: Sliding Window Gaussian Splatting for Volumetric Video Streaming with Arbitrary Length](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07759) (2024)<br><br><sub>efficiency &middot; streaming &middot; native-4dgs &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; real-time &middot; driving</sub> | <ol><li>Enables training, delivering, and rendering volumetric video in a real-time streaming fashion.</li><li>Reduces transmission costs by 83.6% compared to previous work and could be easily scaled to volumetric videos with arbitrary length with no increasing of required GPU resources.</li></ol> |
| [Compact 3D Gaussian Splatting for Static and Dynamic Radiance Fields](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03822) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://maincold2.github.io/c3dgs/ "Project page")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; compression &middot; real-time</sub> | <ol><li>Introduces a learnable mask strategy that reduces the number of Gaussians while preserving high performance.</li><li>Introduces a compact but effective representation of view-dependent color by employing a grid-based neural field rather than relying on spherical harmonics.</li><li>Learns codebooks to compactly represent the geometric and temporal attributes by residual vector quantization.</li></ol> |
| [LGS: A Light-weight 4D Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Surgical Scene Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16073) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://lgs-endo.github.io/ "Project page")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; compression &middot; real-time &middot; endoscopy-surgery &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; monocular</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>LGS, a lightweight 4D Gaussian Splatting framework for dynamic endoscopic reconstruction that cuts storage by more than 9x while keeping rendering quality and real-time speed.</li><li>Deformation-Aware Pruning: a per-Gaussian deformation score over all pixels and timestamps splits Gaussians into stable and deformed sets, each pruned by its own importance score.</li><li>Gaussian-Attribute Pruning that truncates high-degree SH coefficients with distillation, and Feature Field Condensation that lowers the resolution of the 4D spatiotemporal encoder.</li></ol> |
| [3DGStream: On-the-Fly Training of 3D Gaussians for Efficient Streaming of Photo-Realistic Free-Viewpoint Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01444) (2024)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://sjojok.top/3dgstream/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SJoJoK/3DGStream "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; online &middot; streaming &middot; fast-training &middot; real-time</sub> | <ol><li>Uses a compact Neural Transformation Cache to predict per-frame Gaussian translations and rotations instead of independently optimizing every primitive.</li><li>Adds Gaussians adaptively for newly appearing content while carrying the transformed representation forward through the stream.</li><li>Approximately 12-second per-frame reconstruction and 200 FPS rendering for multi-view free-viewpoint video.</li></ol> |
| [HiFi4G: High-Fidelity Human Performance Rendering via Compact Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03461) (2023)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://nowheretrix.github.io/HiFi4G/ "Project page")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; multi-view &middot; human &middot; compression &middot; tracking &middot; native-4dgs</sub> | <ol><li>Combines Gaussian splatting with non-rigid tracking through a coarse deformation graph and fine Gaussian graph.</li><li>Optimizes a 4D Gaussian representation with adaptive spatial-temporal regularization for dense human-performance footage.</li><li>Introduces residual-compensated compression for compact playback-oriented representations.</li></ol> |
| [A Compact Dynamic 3D Gaussian Representation for Real-Time Dynamic View Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12897) (2023)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://compactdynamic3dgaussian.github.io/ "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/raven38/EfficientDynamic3DGaussian "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>efficiency &middot; monocular &middot; multi-view &middot; per-scene &middot; compression &middot; real-time</sub> | <ol><li>Models Gaussian positions and rotations as compact functions of time while keeping scale, color, and opacity invariant.</li><li>Reduces representation memory and relaxes the dense multi-view observation requirement of per-timestep dynamic Gaussians.</li><li>Supports monocular and multi-view reconstruction while reporting 118 FPS at 1,352 by 1,014 resolution on a single GPU.</li></ol> |

monocular and multi-view input remains in the multi-view category.

| [EdMCGS: Event-Driven Markov Chain Gaussian Splatting for Extreme-Low-Frame-Rate Dynamic Scene Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08332) (2026)<br><br>[![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/joseclipse/EdMCGS "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; sparse-frame &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; real-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Casts scene motion as an event-driven Markov chain whose transition, driven by each interval's events, stays active at inference rather than interpolating (elsarticle-template-num.tex:205-217).</li><li>Drives that chain by local event sampling: each control point reads its own motion code from the accumulated event map at its image projection (elsarticle-template-num.tex:224-232).</li><li>Adds a temporal local isometry regularizer preserving inter-point distances across nearby deformed timestamps, keeping propagated motion locally rigid without estimating rotations (elsarticle-template-num.tex:239-250).</li></ol> |
| [SMG: Semantic Motion Graph for Monocular Dynamic Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.31023) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://smg-gaussian.github.io/ "Project page")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; uncertainty &middot; dataset</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: method</sub> | <ol><li>Semantic Motion Graph: a graph on lifted 2D tracks whose edges join only trajectory-level KNN neighbours passing a DINOv3 cosine gate, so Gaussian motion propagates within a semantic group (sec/3_method.tex:31-41).</li><li>Confidence-aware ARAP and local rigid motion control: per-frame node confidence asymmetrically weights ARAP edges so reliable nodes steer unreliable ones, while LRM penalises local velocity no rigid twist explains (sec/3_method.tex:95-115).</li><li>The SMG Dataset: a real-world ego-exo capture pairing a moving egocentric with a static exocentric camera, with PnP poses and Depth Anything 3 metric depth (sec/4_experiments.tex:262-267).</li></ol> |
| [Stochastic Liquid Deformation Fields: An SDE Generalisation of Closed-Form Continuous-Time Cells for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28702) (2026)<br><br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; continuous-time</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>Adding one Gaussian increment to each CfC cell's time-gate pre-activation restores the diffusion the closed form drops: no solver, no parameters, training-only, and exactly the CfC at lambda=0 (main.tex:143-148).</li><li>Evaluation of the liquid field, with and without noise, against a matched Deformable-3DGS MLP on D-NeRF and NeRF-DS, plus a deformation-field parameter-count comparison measured with ptflops (main.tex:230-245).</li><li>A calibrated negative result: against a measured 0.05 dB run-to-run spread, small lambda leaves the D-NeRF mean unchanged and larger lambda lowers it, while NeRF-DS prefers lambda=0 (main.tex:247-249).</li></ol> |
| [LaGSplat: Inferring Physics-Governed Interactive Simulation from Monocular Video Using Latent Lagrangian Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16324) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://louenpottier.github.io/lagsplat.html "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/LouenPottier/LaGSplat "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; physics-aware &middot; explicit &middot; real-time &middot; robotics</sub> | <ol><li>Each primitive's map from q to its centre is affine with a constant Jacobian, so a force applied at inference pulls back as J-transpose f into the learned equations of motion without retraining.</li><li>On the two-segment pneumatic robot of Krauss et al., evaluated on the authors' own data, split and protocol, it reports the lowest MSE of the five models compared, with four latent coordinates against ten.</li></ol> |
| [AdaAnchor4D: Anchor-Conditioned Spatiotemporal Feature Aggregation for Monocular UAV 4D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28320) (2026)<br><br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; aerial &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; real-time</sub> | <ol><li>Adapts shared spatiotemporal features to heterogeneous monocular UAV scenes with anchor-conditioned feature aggregation.</li><li>Separates anchor-state motion from local Gaussian geometry through decoupled local deformation.</li><li>Warps feature-query coordinates according to non-uniform anchor density and evaluates on UAV-Arc4D, VisDrone, and UAVDT.</li></ol> |
| [Progressive Pose-Guided 4D Animal Reconstruction from Monocular Video](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00157) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://syl-322.github.io/ReWild4D/ "Project page")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>A progressive test-time optimisation framework reconstructing 4D animals from one monocular video with 3D Gaussians, needing no annotated data, template or generative prior; the shape prior is only a coarse initialisation (sec/1_intro.tex:30).</li><li>A two-stage pipeline disentangling articulated pose from non-rigid deformation: a symmetry-aware temporal encoding absorbs camera drift, and learnable part anchors drive pose estimation and condition a cross-attention deformation module (sec/1_intro.tex:32-33).</li><li>On Artemis it reports 24.027 dB PSNR, 0.065 LPIPS, 0.0156 CD/diag and F@1% 0.439, the best value in every column of tab:artemis_compare against D-3DGS\* and GART\* (tables/ablation.tex:24-26).</li></ol> |

| [ArtiTwinSplat: Interactable Digital Twin Reconstruction via Gaussian Splatting from RGB-D videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24628) (2026)<br><br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; rgb-d &middot; monocular &middot; robotics &middot; explicit &middot; per-scene</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>ArtiTwinSplat: a four-stage pipeline turning a static pre-change RGB-D sequence and a dynamic post-change RGB-D video into an articulated, photorealistic 3DGS digital twin without CAD, labels or annotation.</li><li>Unsupervised articulation discovery: change detection plus SAM2 part masks, TAPIP3D 3D point tracks, and 4D RANSAC fitting of revolute or prismatic joint type, axis, pivot, per-frame variable and range.</li><li>Articulation-conditioned two-phase Gaussian optimization that transforms part Gaussians by the recovered joint per frame, then refines global radiance; export to URDF for Isaac Sim.</li></ol> |
| [Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23688) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://lift4d.github.io "Project page") [![Functional GitHub repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/-1f883d?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/yehonathanlitman/Lift4D "Functional GitHub repository")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; depth-prior</sub> | <ol><li>Causal latent conditioning turns a frozen image-to-3D model into a 4D prior without retraining, warm-starting each frame's flow-matching ODE from the previous frame's clean latent (sec/3_methodology.tex:45-57; t_0 = 0.2 at sec/X_sup.tex:32-33).</li><li>Per-frame reconstructions are distilled into canonical 3D Gaussians plus a deformation MLP over 1024 sparse control nodes, each predicting a per-frame SE(3) transform applied by linear blend skinning (sec/3_methodology.tex:63-86; sec/X_sup.tex:7-20).</li><li>An occlusion-aware appearance stage composites a colour-matched rendering into occluded pixels and regularises unobserved surface with a Stable Zero123 score-distillation loss conditioned on that completed reference (sec/3_methodology.tex:93-121).</li></ol> |
| [ManiSplat: Manipulation Trajectory Synthesis from Monocular Video via Decoupled 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10645) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://whhu7.github.io/ManiSplat/ "Project page")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; explicit &middot; robotics</sub><br><sub>⚠ unverified: experiments</sub> | <ol><li>A Gaussian scene graph composes each time step as G(t) = G_bg union G_robot(t) union {G_obj^v(t)}, keeping robot and objects as separately controllable Gaussian subfields over a static background (sec/3_method.tex:39-48).</li><li>Task-oriented alignment splits a demonstration into Skill and Motion phases by end-effector-to-object distance, then builds a pseudo-ground-truth object trajectory from a static, a gripper-attached and a keypoint-registration constraint (sec/3_method.tex:70-101).</li><li>Topology-preserving augmentation rigidly transforms an identified Skill segment together with the end-effector trajectory and re-plans the intervening Motion segments, synthesising new demonstrations from one real video (sec/3_method.tex:142-155).</li></ol> |
| [Liquid Neural Networks as a Drop-in Continuous-Time Deformation Field for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07670) (2026)<br><br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; deformable-3dgs &middot; continuous-time</sub> | <ol><li>Replaces the eight-layer positional-encoded deformation MLP of Deformable 3DGS with a stack of Closed-form Continuous-time (CfC) cells whose sigmoidal time gate makes the field an explicit function of frame time.</li><li>Depth-as-time design: every cell receives t as its elapsed-time signal and the hidden state resets each pass, so no recurrence or ODE solver is needed and the rest of the D-3DGS pipeline is untouched.</li><li>On the eight D-NeRF and seven NeRF-DS scenes the liquid field ties or beats the retrained MLP baseline at 36% fewer parameters and MACs (D=6, W=128).</li></ol> |

| [MonoPhysics: Estimating Geometry, Appearance, and Physical Parameters from Monocular Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30320) (2026)<br><br>[![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/-0969da?logo=googleearth&logoColor=white)](https://daniel03c1.github.io/MonoPhysics/ "Project page")<br><sub>monocular-reconstruction &middot; monocular &middot; per-scene &middot; physics-aware &middot; explicit</sub> | <ol><li>Holds Gaussians in camera space and learns one global scale scalar s, mapped to world space by known extrinsics, so image losses through the differentiable MPM simulation resolve absolute scale (sections/03_method.tex:84-93).</li><li>Refines geometry with physics: per-particle MPM volumes are re-induced from the current particle distribution under partition-of-unity, and particles are relocated by an importance averaging visual and physical terms (sections/03_method.tex:104-155).</li><li>A differentiable position map renders pixel coordinates through 3DGS alpha compositing under stop-gradient, giving pixel-location losses a unit gradient to each Gaussian's 2D mean (sections/03_method.tex:158-179, sections/98_supple.tex:70-92).</li></ol> |
